protocols.name: PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)
protocols.description: DNA amplification by thermocycling through denaturation, annealing, and extension phases. Requires precise temperature control and sealed plates to prevent evaporation.
constraints: Denaturation: 95°C for 30s; Annealing: 50–65°C for 30s; Extension: 72°C for 60s per kb
Maximum 35 cycles recommended — beyond this increases non-specific amplification risk
Use PCR-grade sealed plate (nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt) with thermocycler lid at 105°C
Typical reaction volume: 25–50 µL per well; keep on ice until thermocycler step
Master mix should be prepared fresh and kept cold (4°C) to prevent polymerase degradation
Negative control (no-template) and positive control wells are mandatory
384-well plates reduce reagent cost but require multichannel pipetting precision
protocols.cost_notes: Polymerase enzyme is the dominant cost at $0.08/µL; minimize dead volume with PCR plates

protocols.name: ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay)
protocols.description: Antibody-based detection assay performed in multi-well plates. Requires coating, blocking, primary/secondary antibody incubation, and colorimetric detection steps.
constraints: Coating: 100 µL antigen/well overnight at 4°C or 2h at 37°C — plate must be sealed during incubation
Blocking: 200–300 µL BSA or milk solution for 1h at RT to prevent non-specific binding
Primary antibody incubation: 1–2h at RT or overnight at 4°C — seal plate to prevent evaporation
Washing steps (PBS-T): 3–5× with 300 µL/well — thorough aspiration critical to reduce background
TMB substrate incubation: 15–30 min in the dark; stop with 50 µL 2N H2SO4
Read absorbance at 450 nm within 30 min of stopping
Use flat-bottom plates (corning_96_wellplate_360ul_flat) for optical clarity
High-throughput: 384-well reduces antibody cost significantly but requires precision pipetting
protocols.cost_notes: Antibodies at $0.12/µL are the dominant cost; minimise volumes with 384-well format

protocols.name: DNA Extraction
protocols.description: Isolation of genomic or plasmid DNA from biological samples using lysis, binding, washing, and elution steps. Magnetic bead or column-based workflows on Opentrons.
constraints: Cell lysis buffer must be pre-warmed to 65°C for tissue samples; room temperature for cultured cells
Magnetic bead-based workflows require magnetic module — beads must bind ≥10 min before separation
Wash steps (70% ethanol): perform 2× washes to remove salts and inhibitors
Elution volume: 50–100 µL warm elution buffer (10 mM Tris, pH 8.5); warm increases yield
Proteinase K incubation: 56°C for 30–60 min if processing tissue — use temperature module
Avoid transferring the magnetic bead pellet during elution — pipette from opposite well wall
Expected yield: 10–50 ng/µL for cultured cells; lower for primary tissue
protocols.cost_notes: Lysis buffers are cheap ($0.001/µL); elution buffer dominates volume; beads are reusable

protocols.name: RNA Extraction
protocols.description: Isolation of total RNA with strict RNase-free conditions. Requires guanidinium-based lysis, phase separation or column binding, and DNase treatment.
constraints: All consumables must be certified RNase-free — use dedicated RNase-free tips and plates
Work quickly on ice; RNA degrades rapidly at room temperature
β-mercaptoethanol or DTT must be added to lysis buffer immediately before use
DNase I treatment: 30 min at 37°C to remove genomic DNA contamination
Wash with 80% ethanol (not 70%) for RNA column protocols
Elute in RNase-free water; avoid DEPC-treated water for downstream RT reactions
Quantify by Nanodrop: A260/A280 ≥ 1.8 indicates pure RNA
Store immediately at −80°C; avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles
protocols.cost_notes: Guanidinium lysis reagents are moderately priced; main cost is RNase-free certified consumables

protocols.name: Cell Viability Assay (MTT / CellTiter-Glo)
protocols.description: Quantitative measurement of living cells using metabolic activity (MTT) or ATP luminescence (CellTiter-Glo). Performed in 96- or 384-well plates after drug treatment.
constraints: MTT: Add 10 µL of 5 mg/mL MTT solution per 100 µL culture medium; incubate 2–4h at 37°C
After MTT incubation, aspirate medium and dissolve formazan crystals in 100 µL DMSO per well
Read absorbance at 570 nm (reference 690 nm) within 1h of DMSO addition
CellTiter-Glo: equilibrate reagent to RT for 30 min before use; add 1:1 volume to media
Luminescence signal is stable for ~2h — read promptly
Seal plate edges during drug incubation to prevent edge evaporation effect
Include vehicle control (DMSO ≤0.1%), positive control (staurosporine), and cell-free blank
384-well plates reduce cell and reagent cost; use ≥ 1000 cells/well minimum
protocols.cost_notes: Reagent costs moderate; 384-well format reduces per-sample cost by ~75%

protocols.name: Serial Dilution
protocols.description: Systematic preparation of concentration gradients across a plate for dose-response curves, standard curves, or dilution series.
constraints: Use the same tip for sequential dilution steps only when cross-contamination risk is acceptable
Mix thoroughly (10× pipette up-down) at each dilution step before transferring
For 2-fold serial: transfer 50 µL into 50 µL diluent across columns/rows
For 10-fold serial: transfer 10 µL into 90 µL diluent
Discard tip after final transfer to avoid back-contamination into diluent
Start from lowest concentration if working with viscous samples
Column-wise dilution: use 8-channel pipette to process all rows simultaneously
Final well should contain diluent-only blank
protocols.cost_notes: Tip reuse possible within a dilution series — reduces tip cost significantly

protocols.name: Protein Purification (His-tag / IMAC)
protocols.description: Affinity purification of recombinant proteins using immobilized metal affinity chromatography or magnetic Ni-NTA beads on Opentrons.
constraints: Equilibrate Ni-NTA beads in binding buffer (50 mM NaH2PO4, 300 mM NaCl, 10 mM imidazole, pH 8.0)
Binding incubation: 1h at 4°C with gentle mixing — avoid foaming
Wash: 3× with wash buffer (20 mM imidazole) to remove non-specifically bound proteins
Elution: stepwise imidazole gradient (50, 100, 250, 500 mM) or single-step 250 mM
Keep samples at 4°C throughout using temperature module
Magnetic bead format allows full automation on Opentrons magnetic module
Assess purity by SDS-PAGE after purification
protocols.cost_notes: Imidazole buffers inexpensive; recombinant protein value typically justifies higher reagent investment

protocols.name: NGS Library Prep
protocols.description: Preparation of sequencing libraries from DNA or RNA including fragmentation, end repair, adapter ligation, and PCR amplification steps.
constraints: All steps require RNase/DNase-free reagents and consumables
End repair + A-tailing: 20 min at 65°C — use temperature module
Adapter ligation: 15 min at 20°C; ligase is sensitive to temperature fluctuations
AMPure XP bead cleanup: 0.8× volume beads for 200–500 bp fragment selection
Bead incubation: 5 min at RT followed by 5 min on magnetic module before aspirating
Elute in ≥15 µL low TE to maximize recovery of small fragments
Index PCR: 8–12 cycles maximum to avoid over-amplification bias
Quantify libraries by qPCR or Bioanalyzer before pooling
384-well format suitable for high-throughput library prep (>96 samples)
protocols.optimal_labware: nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt with magnetic module and thermocycler
protocols.cost_notes: Enzyme costs dominate (ligase, polymerase); AMPure beads reusable if handled carefully

protocols.name: Cell Culture Media Preparation and Dispensing
protocols.description: Automated dispensing of cell culture media, supplements, or drugs into multi-well plates for cell-based assays.
constraints: Media must be pre-warmed to 37°C before dispensing — use temperature module at 37°C
Sterile technique required: use filtered tips (opentrons_96_filtertiprack_200ul)
Do not reuse tips across different media types — contamination risk
For drug treatment: prepare master mix in reservoir, then dispense to all wells
FBS-supplemented media: mix gently before dispensing to ensure homogeneity
Aspirate from reservoir not the well bottom to avoid disturbing cell monolayer
Use multi-channel pipette for full plate dispensing to minimize timing variability
Media change timing: consistent across all wells to ensure uniform treatment duration
protocols.cost_notes: Media and buffers at $0.001/µL; filtered tips add cost but prevent cross-contamination

protocols.name: Magnetic Bead-Based Cleanup
protocols.description: Solid-phase reversible immobilization (SPRI) using paramagnetic beads for nucleic acid size selection and purification.
constraints: Equilibrate SPRI beads to room temperature for ≥30 min before use
Add beads at correct volume ratio for target fragment size (0.6× for >400 bp, 1.8× for >100 bp)
Binding incubation: 5 min at room temperature with gentle mixing
Magnetic separation: place on magnetic module for ≥2 min until solution is completely clear
Wash: 2× with 200 µL 80% freshly prepared ethanol — do not disturb bead pellet
Air dry beads: 2–5 min on magnet (not over-dry — beads crack if too dry)
Elution: add buffer away from bead pellet, mix, remove from magnet, incubate 2 min, re-magnetize
Transfer eluate promptly to avoid bead carry-over
protocols.cost_notes: Bead cleanup adds ~5 min robot time; critical for downstream applications
